plan: In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy: you never overpay since you only pay the second-highest bid, and bidding truthfully maximizes expected profit regardless of competitors' strategies. Bidding below value risks losing profitable auctions; bidding above value risks negative profit. With value $25, the optimal bid is exactly $25.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy—it maximizes expected profit regardless of what others bid. If I win, I pay the second-highest bid, not my own bid, so bidding my true value ensures I only win when profitable (value > second-highest bid) and never overpay. There's no incentive to shade the bid here since payment depends on others' bids, not mine. With a value of $18, I should bid exactly $18.

If I win, I pay the second-highest bid (not my own bid), so bidding my true value maximizes expected profit - I never overpay relative to my value, and I win whenever my value exceeds the second-highest bid. There's no benefit to shading my bid in this format. Therefore, I will bid exactly my value of $31.
